title: Gatebraid evidence capture record (gatebraid/evidence-capture@1)
description: The canonical, machine-readable record of ONE command execution captured as evidence. Frozen at M3 batch N1 as one of the three shared interfaces, BEFORE any N2/N3 authoring (M3-PLAN.md §2 N1). The byte contract below is the P0-2 class fixed AT SPECIFICATION and deliberately not left to the implementer: N2 implements this contract, it does not define it, and N3 re-derives verdicts from documents of this shape plus the frozen schemas alone. Markdown renderings of a capture are a DERIVED VIEW and never a second hand-written authority (M3-PLAN.md §2 N2). AMENDED at M3 batch N1C by approved correct-course (M3-PLAN.md §2 N1 routes any interface change through one): four constraints previously read as enforced and were not — the two timestamps now carry enforcing patterns and no longer carry `format`, whose enforcement was measured to depend on the caller and on an installed package, and binary_mode_write and self_assertions.zero_lone_cr.asserted are now `const: true`. The one remaining unenforceable relation, ended_at >= started_at, is named in ended_at's own description as an N3 duty rather than left implicit. The $id is unchanged: this is a correct-course on @1, not a version bump.

capture_id.description: Stable identifier for this capture, referenced by a gate record's checks[].output_ref.

generator.description: Which committed instrument produced this record. A capture whose producer cannot be named cannot be re-run (ADR-0028: committed, falsified, reused).

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the generator source as committed, so the record names the exact instrument, not merely its version string.

invocation.description: argv-form is the default; a shell invocation must declare its platform and exit-code semantics, because `pipefail` and friends decide whether a non-zero exit is even observable (M3-PLAN.md §6, 'wrong pipeline exit code').

form.description: argv: executed directly, no shell involved. shell: a shell interpreted the string, and shell_semantics is then required.

argv.description: The exact argument vector. For form: shell this is the shell and its arguments, the command string included.

pipefail.description: Whether pipefail was in force. False means a pipeline's exit code is its LAST element's, so a failing upstream stage is invisible — a captured exit code of 0 then proves nothing about the upstream command.

exit_code_source.description: What the recorded exit_code actually measures.

cwd.description: cwd identity, not merely a string: two path-resolution domains disagreeing is a live defect class on this host (friction #127).

resolution.description: absolute-verified: resolved to an absolute path and confirmed to exist at capture time.

environment.description: Environment variables the capture declares as relevant, by name and value — a DECLARED SUBSET, never a whole-environment dump. Two independent reasons, neither of them spec §4's unbounded-identifier-listing rule, which is about repository and project identifiers and does not reach here: a full dump grows the record without bound, and it copies whatever secrets the environment happens to hold into a committed artifact. The cap makes 'subset' a property of the document rather than a hope about the implementer.

allOf.$comment: A shell invocation without declared semantics is an exit code nobody can interpret.

exit_code.description: The process exit status. The exit status decides, not the printed text (spec §4).

started_at.description: A2 correct-course (M3 batch N1C). THE PATTERN IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT. `format: date-time` was REMOVED, not kept as an annotation: measured on this host (jsonschema 4.23.0, rfc3339_validator installed), a validator built WITH a FormatChecker rejects a non-timestamp here while one built without accepts it — so retaining the keyword would have left the corpus's own locus set dependent on a caller decision plus an installed package, which is the contingency this correct-course exists to remove. The ruling's stated ground was that format is 'a silent no-op absent an optional dependency'; on this host it is not a no-op, and the conclusion (use a pattern) is right for the portability reason rather than that one. WHAT THIS PATTERN ENFORCES, measured: the RFC3339 LEXICAL FORM only, case-insensitive in the date/time separator and the zone designator as RFC 5234 requires. FIELD RANGES ARE UNCHECKED — a month of 13, an mday of 45, an hour of 99 or an offset of +99:99 all match, as does a calendar-invalid date such as 2026-02-31. Range and calendar validity, and the ordering of this field against ended_at, are N3 re-derivation duties. The trailing anchor is (?![\s\S]) rather than $, because Python's re matches $ before a final newline while ECMA-262 (which JSON Schema specifies) does not; $ would have made the constraint stricter on a conforming validator than on the one this project runs.

ended_at.description: As started_at: the pattern is the only enforcement, `format` is absent for the same measured reason, the check is of lexical form with field ranges unchecked, and the trailing anchor is (?![\s\S]). **`ended_at >= started_at` is NOT expressible in JSON Schema** — it compares two sibling properties and no keyword relates one instance value to another. Recorded here as an explicit N3 re-derivation duty rather than left to look enforced: a capture whose end precedes its start validates against this schema and must be rejected downstream.

inputs.description: Pinned-SHA inputs (#108). Every file the captured command depended on, by path and content hash at capture time.

outputs.description: Files the captured command wrote, by path, content hash and byte length.

platform.description: N2 and N3 must be green on Windows AND WSL (M3-PLAN.md §2), so every capture names the platform it ran on. A dual-platform claim is read from two captures, never asserted by one.

interpreter.description: The exact interpreter, e.g. 'CPython 3.12.2 (C:/Python312/python.exe)'. Two interpreters on this host differ in whether PyYAML exists and whether text-mode writes emit CRLF; naming the interpreter is what makes a validation reproducible (friction #55).

self_assertions.description: Guarded self-checks the generator ran on its OWN output as it wrote (#108, named in ADR-0028 §4). Each is a check that gates the write, not a claim added afterwards. The whole block is REQUIRED on the parent record: if it were optional, a capture silent about the guard and a capture that ran it would be the same document, which is the absent-versus-none_configured conflation ADR-0019 already removed at the check level.

asserted.description: A2 correct-course (M3 batch N1C): `const: true`, not merely a boolean. The previous form let a record state `false` and validate, while this description said false 'is a finding, not a pass' — the finding was expressible and never refused. A capture that did not run the guard is not a conforming capture; the honest way to record one is to not produce the record. The count constraint below still fires independently, so `asserted: false` and `asserted: true, count: 7` fail at distinct loci.

count.description: Lone CR bytes found. Any value above zero must have prevented the write, which is enforced below rather than merely stated.

allOf.$comment: The record exists, so the write happened. asserted:true with count>0 therefore describes a state the guard is defined to make impossible, and a schema that admits it lets a generator report a guard it overrode.

binary_mode_write.description: A2 correct-course (M3 batch N1C): `const: true`, not merely a boolean. The previous form let a record state `false` and validate, while this description said text mode 'would silently invalidate every byte_length and sha256 above' — a constraint that read as enforced and was not. The record exists, so the write happened; if it happened in text mode the digests above are already wrong and the document is not a capture. Same reasoning as zero_lone_cr above.

byteStream.description: THE BYTE CONTRACT (M3-PLAN.md §2 N2, the P0-2 remedy). A captured stream is carried as base64 of its RAW BYTES. The JSON document itself is UTF-8 and no raw byte is ever embedded directly in a JSON string — that is what made the producer/consumer contract inconsistent in the M2 tools, where the producer wrote platform-encoded stdout and the consumer forced UTF-8 (ADR-0029 decision 2, P0-2; friction #60). Any human-readable form of this stream lives in `rendered` and is DERIVED, never authoritative.

encoding.description: Fixed. There is exactly one encoding, so no consumer has to negotiate.

byte_length.description: Length of the RAW bytes before base64, not the length of `data`.

sha256.description: SHA-256 over the RAW bytes before base64, so a consumer can confirm the stream it decoded is the stream that was captured.

data.description: Standard base64 of the raw bytes. Empty string for an empty stream. The pattern is the length-correct base64 grammar, not a character-class filter: a filter admits undecodable strings such as "A" or "=", and this is the field the byte contract rests on. Re-deriving sha256 and byte_length from these bytes is NOT expressible in JSON Schema; that obligation belongs to the independent validator and is stated in N3's acceptance criteria, not asserted here.

rendered.description: DERIVED VIEW ONLY — never authoritative, and never the thing a verdict is read from. It exists so a human can read the capture without decoding it by hand, and it records honestly when the decode did not round-trip.

decode_codec.description: The codec attempted, e.g. 'utf-8' or 'cp936'. cp936 is this host's console default and the round trip through it is a §6 fixture class.

decode_result.description: ok: clean round trip. replaced: decoded with replacement characters, so `text` is LOSSY and differs from the bytes. failed: no text produced.

decode_error.description: Required whenever decode_result is not ok.

text.description: The decoded text. Absent when decode_result is failed. Present-but-lossy when replaced — which is why it is never authoritative.

allOf.$comment: A non-clean decode that does not say what went wrong is a silent lossy render — the class this field exists to prevent.
A failed decode cannot also carry text.
A replaced decode MUST carry the lossy text. Without this, 'replaced' can be recorded with nothing to inspect, and the reader cannot see what was lost.

A clean decode carries its text and CANNOT carry an error: 'ok' plus decode_error is a self-contradicting record. M3-PLAN §2 N2 names decode_codec, decode_result AND decode_error as the derived field's contents; making decode_error conditional on a non-clean result is a deliberate narrowing, recorded here rather than left silent, because a clean decode has no error to report and a required-but-empty field invites a placeholder.
